title: Prompt telemetry micro-PRD and instrumention scribble
body:
Goal:
- Lightweight, privacy-first prompt-level telemetry to help engineers debug prompt regressions, understand cost/latency by prompt variant, and power simple A/B rollouts of prompt templates without shipping whole-model changes.

Motivation / problem statements:
- We get noisy bug reports: "responses got worse" but customers rarely provide the exact prompt or variant.
- Hard to tie regressions to prompt changes vs model upgrades vs routing.
- No easy way to measure token-cost per prompt template across real traffic samples.
- Need minimal surface area: customers often balk at heavy observability changes.

High-level product idea:
- Instrument SDK + API to attach a short, user-provided prompt_label (string) and optional prompt_hash (client-side) to each request.
- Server-side sampling and derived metrics: median latency, p50/p95 token usage, error rate, avg tokens per role, top n-gram hallucination signals (optional, opt-in).
- Console: prompt-telemetry view (per-API-key) that lists active labels, quick trends, day-over-day cost delta for a label, and a small diff view for variants (A/B).
- Rollout helper: ability to map a label to a rollout percentage and see live effect on cost/latency.

Minimal instrumentation spec (initial MVP):
- SDK: add optional param prompt_metadata: {label: string, sample_rate: float (0..1)}. If sample_rate omitted default to 0.05. (We will only accept flat string/number fields from client.)
- REST API accept header X-Prompt-Label (max 64 chars) or query param prompt_label. Server will respect privacy rules (no storing full prompt text unless customer opts in; just store label + derived aggregates).
- Storage: aggregated time-series per (api_key, label, model_family, day, hour) with fields: requests_count, tokens_in, tokens_out, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, errors_count. No raw prompt text stored.

User stories:
- As an SRE, I want to quickly see which prompt labels spiked error rate after a deploy so I can triage rollback decisions.
- As a PM, I want cost delta for a new prompt template so I can estimate downstream billing impact before full rollout.
- As an eng on a customer engagement, I want to map a customer's prompt labels to their API key usage to show savings after optimization.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- SDK and HTTP header accepted and sampled telemetry shows up in metrics within 10 minutes.
- Console shows top 20 labels by traffic for the last 7 days with cost and latency deltas.
- Telemetry data respects privacy defaults (no raw prompt string saved).
- On-by-default sampling rate <= 5% for new customer keys; customers can opt into full-capture via org setting and DPA.

Privacy & compliance considerations:
- Default: do NOT persist prompt text. Only store label + hashed prompt_id if provided by customer.
- Offer an explicit "capture_prompts" org-level feature flag for enterprise customers with DPA/contract. When enabled, prompts stored encrypted with customer-managed KMS.
- Must document data retention: default 30 days for per-label aggregates, 90 days for enterprise with opt-in, with ability to purge on request.

Instrumentation edge cases / constraints:
- Label collisions: encourage namespacing (team/myflow-chat-v1). Console should surface examples of top labels but never show raw prompts unless capture_prompts enabled.
- Label spamming: rate-limit unique labels per key (e.g., 1,000 unique labels/day) to avoid cardinality explosion.
- Backwards compatibility: fall back silently if header not recognized.

Console UI sketches (text):
- List view: label | requests/day | tokens/day | cost delta 7d | p95 latency | error rate | last seen
- Label detail: small sparkline + rolling sample table (if capture enabled) + quick diff: variant A vs B by metric.
- Quick action: "promote label to rollout" -> opens rollout modal to send 10/25/50/100% traffic to label or apply only to a given model family/region.

Rollout mechanics (rough):
- Rollout by label is client-side via SDK variant selection OR server-side via routing rules. Console will write a rollout config that maps percentages to backend variants.
- For MVP, implement conservative server-side routing: if label-rollout config exists, route matching requests deterministically by hash(api_key, request_id) to variant, else default.

Metrics & SLOs:
- Telemetry pipeline latency: <15 minutes end-to-end for sampled events in MVP.
- Cardinality control: monitor unique-labels per org and alert >5000/day.

Risks / open questions:
- How to surface useful signal for hallucination without PII? (maybe include model-derived hallucination flags returned by an opt-in_eval microservice).
- Storage cost vs value: aggregates only reduce cost, but some customers will want full capture. Need pricing or plan gating.
- SDK adoption: how to nudge customers to add labels? Provide templates, instrumentation snippets for common frameworks (node/python).

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Engineering: quick spike to add X-Prompt-Label header support + sample pipeline (Ravi) — 2w spike.
- Product: write short customer-facing one-pager explaining default privacy stance and enterprise opt-ins (Imani) — 1w.
- Design: console mockups for label list + rollout modal (Design lead TBD) — 1.5w.
- Legal/security: draft KMS + retention language for enterprise opt-in.

Low-effort adoption nudges (growth):
- Add small example to quickstart: "instrument a chat flow with prompt_label='support/faq-v2'".
- Provide a preflight check in Console that flags high-cost labels and suggests token-saving tips (trim system prompt, compress history).

Notes to self / things to track later:
- Consider a small client-side helper to compute stable prompt_hash (sha1 of normalized prompt) so users can track variants without storing text.
- Investigate correlation of labels with dedicated capacity tiers (do some labels disproportionately hit dedicated pools?).
- Pattern library of recommended label names and examples to avoid anti-patterns (e.g., full user text as label).

Slack threads / tickets to link when this doc moves: #telemetry, #hosting-rollouts, RED-1192 (backend sampling), SDK-482 (node sdk header patch).

-- end of scribble --

(keeping intentionally terse — this is a personal parking lot; will expand into proper PRD if we get buy-in)
